doc.title: Milt Hinton interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

title: Hamilton honors, Doc Cheatham and Clark Terry, and goodbyes
summary: They thank each other, discuss Hamilton's honors for Hinton, Doc Cheatham and Clark Terry, and sign off.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: So beautiful to be here, Joe.

Yeah, but you, your time up at Hamilton. That was so delicious, though. Milt, you know, Fillius, he’s the man, he’s the man, one of the Trustees at Hamilton. And he has done wonderful things, up there, to honor you. But I’ve got an idea, too. I think if Doc Cheatham would just hold on a couple more years, I think we ought to get him too.
Cause I don’t believe what he has done.
You’re kidding me. Oh my gosh.
He’s amazing, absolutely amazing. And he’s playing now, not fooling around, he’s playing.
I know. I know he’s playing. You know it’s difficult I imagine.
I was walking down the street with him in Nice, France one day at the Nice festival. He said, “I was in a restaurant here in 1923.” I was in the sixth grade.

I was a baby. I was, I don’t know if it was on camera, at the college at commencement when they honored Clark Terry this year, and it was real, real big fun. I had a chance to tell him now he’s a collared Fellow, with the hood on. You are now officially a collared Fellow. Dr. Terry.
Thank you for giving the precious gift of our time.
Thank you. It’s been “nighty mice,” as Jo Jones used to say.
Jo, yeah. I think he stole that from Basie.
